meta.title: Upper/Lower Muscle Plan
meta.goal: Maximise muscle growth; lean out gradually

upperA.name: Upper A
upperA.warmup: 5 min easy cardio, then 2–3 ramp-up sets of incline press (about 50%, 70%, 85% of your working weight for 8, 5, 2 reps). One light feeler set before each new movement after that.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell press
exercises.cue: Lower until the dumbbells are beside your chest and you feel a deep stretch; elbows about 45° from your sides.
exercises.swap: Incline machine press or Smith incline press
exercises.why: A heavy press while you are fresh. The incline loads the upper chest and front delts, so no separate overhead press is needed.

exercises.name: Chest-supported row
exercises.cue: Let the shoulder blades spread fully at the bottom, then pull elbows back at about 45–60°.
exercises.swap: Seated machine row or one-arm dumbbell row
exercises.why: Chest support removes the lower back as the limiting factor, so the upper back and lats reach a hard effort.

exercises.name: Lat pulldown
exercises.cue: Full hang at the top with arms straight; pull elbows down to your sides without leaning far back.
exercises.why: A vertical pull to pair with the row, so the lats are trained through shoulder adduction as well as extension.

exercises.name: Pec deck
exercises.cue: Set the seat so your arms open wide; pause for a second in the stretch on every rep.
exercises.swap: Cable fly or dumbbell fly on a low incline
exercises.why: Chest work with no triceps involvement, loaded hardest where the chest is longest.

exercises.name: Cable lateral raise
exercises.detail: one arm, cable at hand height
exercises.cue: Start with the hand slightly across your body; raise out and a little forward to shoulder height. Go straight from one arm to the other.
exercises.why: Side delts only grow from direct work. The cable keeps tension at the bottom, where a dumbbell has none.

exercises.name: Overhead cable triceps extension
exercises.cue: Elbows stay up beside your head; let the hands travel far behind you for a full stretch.
exercises.why: Arms overhead puts the long head of the triceps at length; a 12-week trial found more triceps growth this way than with pushdowns.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell curl
exercises.cue: Let the arms hang straight down behind your torso; curl without the elbows drifting forward.
exercises.swap: Cable curl facing away from the stack
exercises.why: Trains the biceps from a stretched position, complementing the preacher curl on Upper B.

lowerA.name: Lower A
lowerA.warmup: 5 min bike, then 3 ramp-up sets on the hack squat (about 40%, 60%, 80% of working weight for 8, 5, 3 reps). Two lighter sets before Romanian deadlifts.

exercises.name: Hack squat
exercises.detail: as deep as you can control
exercises.cue: Feet low enough on the plate that your knees travel well forward; controlled descent, no bounce.
exercises.swap: High-bar back squat, pendulum squat or Smith squat
exercises.why: A stable machine squat lets the quads, not balance or the lower back, decide when the set ends.

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
exercises.cue: Push the hips back with soft knees until the hamstrings are fully stretched (bar around mid-shin); keep the bar against your legs.
exercises.swap: Dumbbell RDL or 45° back extension with load
exercises.why: The main hip hinge: heavy load on hamstrings and glutes at long length. Kept a little further from failure because fatigue from this lift is high.

exercises.name: Leg extension
exercises.cue: Recline the backrest and keep your hips down; pause briefly at the top.
exercises.why: Squats and presses grow the rectus femoris poorly; leg extensions cover it, and leaning back trained it better in a 10-week trial.

exercises.name: Seated leg curl
exercises.cue: Lean the torso slightly forward and hold the handles; control the weight all the way back to straight legs.
exercises.why: Sitting flexes the hip, so the hamstrings work at longer lengths; a 12-week trial found more growth seated than lying.

exercises.name: Standing calf raise
exercises.cue: Sink into the bottom and hold the stretch for 1–2 s on every rep. When full reps fail, keep going with bottom-half reps.
exercises.swap: Calf raise on the leg press or Smith machine
exercises.why: Straight knees keep the gastrocnemius long; calf studies favour the stretched half of the rep.

exercises.name: Cable crunch
exercises.cue: Round the spine and bring ribs toward pelvis; hips stay still.
exercises.why: Abs are trained like any other muscle: loaded, in a moderate rep range, with load added over time.

upperB.name: Upper B
upperB.warmup: 5 min easy cardio, then 2 ramp-up sets of pulldowns or band-assisted pull-ups, and 2 ramp-up sets before the chest press.

exercises.name: Pull-up
exercises.detail: add weight once you pass 10 reps
exercises.cue: Start every rep from a dead hang; chin clearly over the bar.
exercises.swap: Lat pulldown with a wider grip than on Upper A
exercises.why: The heaviest back work of the week goes first on this day, mirroring the press-first order of Upper A.
exercises.weightHint: Leave kg empty for body weight only, or enter the weight you added.

exercises.name: Machine chest press
exercises.cue: Set the seat so the handles line up with mid-chest; let them come back as far as your shoulders allow.
exercises.swap: Dumbbell bench press or barbell bench press
exercises.why: A second heavy press at a different angle from Monday's incline.

exercises.name: Seated cable row
exercises.detail: wide or neutral grip, to lower chest
exercises.cue: Reach forward and let the shoulder blades spread; pull the elbows out and back, no torso swing.
exercises.why: A wider pull than the chest-supported row, shifting work toward the upper back and rear delts.

exercises.name: Low-to-high cable fly
exercises.cue: Step forward so the cables pull your arms back and down; sweep up and in to chin height.
exercises.why: Brings weekly chest volume to 11 sets without adding more triceps and elbow stress.

exercises.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
exercises.cue: Lean very slightly forward, lead with the elbows, stop at shoulder height.
exercises.why: Second weekly dose for the side delts, in a higher rep range.

exercises.name: Reverse pec deck
exercises.cue: Arms nearly straight, sweep out wide; don't squeeze the shoulder blades together hard.
exercises.swap: Cable rear-delt fly or face pull
exercises.why: Direct rear-delt work; rows alone leave them under-trained.

exercises.name: Preacher curl
exercises.cue: Lower until the arms are almost straight; the bottom half is the part that counts.
exercises.swap: Dumbbell preacher curl, one arm at a time
exercises.why: Hardest at the bottom of the rep, where the biceps is long.

exercises.name: Triceps pushdown
exercises.cue: Elbows pinned to your sides; lock out fully.
exercises.why: Elbow-friendly volume for the lateral and medial heads, alongside Monday's overhead work.

lowerB.name: Lower B
lowerB.focus: Hamstring and glute-led, with single-leg work
lowerB.warmup: 5 min bike. The leg curls double as a knee warm-up, so only 1–2 light sets are needed before them, then 2 ramp-up sets on the leg press.

exercises.name: Seated leg curl
exercises.cue: Slightly heavier than on Lower A; same forward lean and controlled return.
exercises.why: Hamstrings first on this day, while they are fresh; it also warms up the knees before the leg press.

exercises.name: Leg press
exercises.cue: Lower until your thighs are close to your chest without the hips rolling off the pad.
exercises.why: Heavy quad work with little demand on the lower back, three days after the hack squat.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
exercises.cue: Long stride, lean the torso slightly forward, sink until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
exercises.swap: Smith machine reverse lunge or walking lunge
exercises.why: Single-leg work loads the glutes and quads deeply and evens out left-right differences.

exercises.name: 45° back extension
exercises.cue: Pad just below the hips; hinge down to a full hamstring stretch and drive the hips into the pad to come up.
exercises.why: A second hip-extension movement for glutes and hamstrings that costs far less fatigue than another deadlift.
exercises.weightHint: Leave kg empty for body weight only, or enter the weight you added.

exercises.name: Leg extension
exercises.cue: Take both sets to the point where you cannot complete another full rep.
exercises.why: Safe to take to failure, and tops up the rectus femoris.

exercises.name: Leg-press calf raise
exercises.cue: Let the plate push your toes back into a deep stretch; pause 1–2 s there.
exercises.why: Second weekly calf session, same stretched-position emphasis.

exercises.name: Hanging leg raise
exercises.cue: Curl the pelvis up toward the ribs; don't just swing the legs.
exercises.swap: Captain's chair knee raise or lying reverse crunch
exercises.why: Trains the abs from the pelvis end, complementing the cable crunch.
exercises.weightHint: Leave kg empty for body weight only, or enter the weight you added.

day5.name: Day 5 (optional)
day5.focus: Zone 2 cardio, core and small muscles
day5.warmup: No separate warm-up; the cardio comes first.

exercises.name: Zone 2 cardio
exercises.cue: A pace at which you can still speak in full sentences (roughly 60–70% of max heart rate).
exercises.why: Builds fitness and adds energy expenditure with almost no recovery cost. Low-impact options interfere least with leg growth.

exercises.name: Ab wheel rollout
exercises.cue: Ribs down, slight posterior pelvic tilt; roll out only as far as you can without the lower back sagging.
exercises.why: Third weekly ab session, loading the abs at long length.
exercises.weightHint: Leave kg empty for body weight only, or enter the weight you added.

exercises.name: Lateral raise
exercises.cue: Same technique as in the upper sessions.
exercises.why: Side delts recover quickly and respond to extra volume; this takes them from 6 to 9 weekly sets.

exercises.name: Face pull
exercises.cue: Pull the rope apart toward your ears, elbows high.
exercises.why: Extra rear-delt and shoulder-rotator work to balance all the pressing.

exercises.name: Hammer curl
exercises.cue: Neutral grip, no swing.
exercises.why: Brachialis and forearm work the main sessions don't cover directly.

exercises.name: Overhead triceps extension
exercises.cue: Same technique as on Upper A.
exercises.why: A little more long-head triceps work if arms are a priority.

exercises.name: Side plank
exercises.cue: Straight line from head to heels; hips forward.
exercises.why: Obliques and trunk stiffness for the heavy squats and hinges.
